row.consequences_md: Every scheduler and override validates against it. Never relax it to rescue a slot. Retire or hold instead.
row.context_md: The core promise is that nobody works on a track twice.
row.decision_md: Record (track, participant) on claim/receipt, submit, and claim-then-skip. Do not record a pre-claim skip or expired offer. Exclude the owner separately. Never reset during the event.

row.consequences_md: Commit-reveal is possible. Groups layer on the same primitive. Infeasible rounds return a conflict list.
row.context_md: Need fair no-repeat schedules without a predictable cyclic pattern.
row.decision_md: Build row by row with a seeded perfect matching. Exclude the owner. Validate no repeats. Default N-1 rounds with an overcrowding warning above 12 participants.
row.title: Classic scheduling uses a randomized partial Latin rectangle

row.consequences_md: Simpler async state and less leak surface. Better reach and fewer repeat pairs. Optional content tags can come later.
row.context_md: The async simulation compared global queue, soft migration, barriers, generational queues, group-aware pools, and a social-diversity objective.
row.decision_md: Use one global queue with a social-diversity objective. Do not use participant groups, migration, barriers, or reserved queues. Classic mode keeps groups.
row.title: Async mode uses no formal groups

row.consequences_md: Faster events, fewer expired offers, lower p95 wait. Edit completeness is not promised. Full exposure takes months at large N.
row.context_md: The async simulation measured claim expiry, release timing, and completeness.
row.decision_md: Default claim window 24h with a 12h reminder. One daily release window with two dispatch waves. Completeness means exposure. Default length N-1 for 12 or fewer participants; 6-8 rounds above 12. Host can choose full exposure.
row.title: 24h claim window, two daily waves, exposure completeness

row.consequences_md: Events finish without chasing people. Some pairs remain unexposed and appear in the gap report. Credits are preserved.
row.context_md: Exposure completeness can loop forever if a participant never claims.
row.decision_md: Offer only to Ready participants. After an expiry, never offer the same track to the same person again. Apply a host-configured strike/cooldown policy. Report exposure gaps. A claimed deadline miss counts as seen.
row.title: Async anti-loop protection

row.consequences_md: The scheduler has N-1 exchange rounds. Plan and assignment rows use the display round number 2..N. Every surface derives the seed round from the round type, not from a minus-one offset. The commitment covers the R1 owner map.
row.context_md: The engine treats seed intake as a pre-round phase and calls the first exchange R1. The event length and file versions both collide with the round number.
row.decision_md: Round 1 is the seed round. Rounds 2..N are exchange rounds. A full-exposure classic event with N seeded participants has N total rounds. File versions use v1..vN. The host opens R1 explicitly with the pack and a seed deadline (default 7 days). The host planner shows a host-only R1 seed band. Participant-visible schedules start at R2.
row.title: Classic rounds start at the seed

row.consequences_md: Start commits and announces the schedule. Opening R2 is a separate host action. Deadline moves do not create a new commitment. The host can reopen one submitted assignment explicitly.
row.context_md: The engine has no round table, no shared deadline, and gives each claim its own edit window. Seed intake opens implicitly at event creation.
row.decision_md: The host explicitly opens R1, then closes seed intake softly and locks the roster in one atomic action with at least two seeds. Seeds after the deadline wait for host approval. Reopen R1 is allowed before commit. Each round has one shared deadline set at open. Offers expire at that deadline and a claim uses the same deadline. Defaults are 7 days for R1, 24 hours for a normal exchange round, and 48 hours for the final exchange round. The host can move a whole round deadline for all offered, claimed, and overdue assignments, preserve individual extensions, return overdue to claimed, re-arm reminders, notify holders, and write one audit entry. Later planned rounds and the reveal shift by the same delta. Submitted work stays final.
row.title: Classic round lifecycle and shared deadlines

row.consequences_md: Participant DTOs never carry owner IDs, group labels, or the full matrix unless open schedule is on. Stream-safe mode must redact the planner and people views, not only the reveal presenter.
row.context_md: A full participant-visible matrix plus full exposure is an owner oracle: each row's missing track is that person's seed.
row.decision_md: Participants see only their own assignments by default. They do not see group membership, group labels, song numbers, seed owners, titles, or comments before the reveal. The host can enable an open schedule. Open schedule means full transparency: the R2..RN matrix, seed owners, editor names, titles, and comments. The host sees a strong warning and the join card discloses the zero-anonymity exception. The R1 seed band is always host-only.
row.title: Own assignments by default; open schedule is the only anonymity exception

row.consequences_md: The app computes editors per track from songs and claims and warns when the value is fractional. The gap report separates exposure gaps from edit gaps. Async credits use a handoff index, never a round label.
row.context_md: Async exposure is over-determined when the host sets songs, claims per person, and editors per track independently. The engine reuses classic rounds for async.
row.decision_md: Async has its own seed intake, separate from classic R1. The host sets expected songs and claims per participant. One track per seeder, so the seeded participant count equals the track count. The host explicitly closes intake and starts the queue. Fewer seeds: the host waits or explicitly shrinks or reserves. Late seeds are off by default; the host can enable them with a feasibility check and a minimum claim quota. Claim and edit windows default to 24 hours each, are set per event, and lock at queue start. After start the host can extend a single offer, never shorten one or change the global window. Async uses handoffs, not synchronized rounds, and has no final round. First expired offer gives a 24-hour cooldown, then a re-offer. A second expiry pauses the participant until Ready or a host action. Expiry does not mark a pair seen and the pair is never re-offered. A claim marks the pair seen.
row.title: Async intake, targets, windows, and expiry

row.consequences_md: Classic no longer silently ignores max_handoffs. The planner shows coverage gaps for flexible events. Async uses the same budget for extra handoffs.
row.context_md: The join flow collects max_handoffs, defaults to 4, and the classic scheduler ignores it. Full exposure for six people needs five exchange edits.
row.decision_md: The seed is not an edit and never consumes the max_handoffs budget. The host chooses per event between strict full exposure and flexible participation. Strict mode requires every active participant to have max_handoffs at least N-1; the host must raise a low budget, bench the person as a fill-in, or switch modes before R1 closes. Flexible mode gives each participant their earliest exchange rounds up to their budget, leaves gaps for the rounds they skip, and the host fills gaps with fill-ins or manual edits. Participants do not request specific tracks; the host edits the plan manually. Date-driven availability is a separate feature and can combine with either mode.
row.title: max_handoffs modes and the seed budget

row.reason_md: The settings store group count and size, but the planner does not suggest groups or warn about soft bounds.
row.solution_idea_md: Add deterministic lookup rules, validation warnings, and plan metadata. Add Gherkin and unit tests. Wire the warnings into the planner data.
row.title: Group lookup, soft bounds, and planner warnings

row.description_md: The planner must rotate participants between groups at each phase boundary. Tracks stay in their original group. The default cadence is K about T divided by 4, with 3 to 5 phases. The plan must keep no repeat, no own track, and one holder per track in every round. Group membership must stay hidden from participants.
row.purpose_md: Large classic events stay varied and feasible.
row.reason_md: The current scheduler ignores the group settings.
row.solution_idea_md: Add a group schedule model to swap-core. Generate each phase within groups with the selected strategy. Rotate participants. Validate global no-repeat. Persist group and phase metadata. Add property and deterministic tests.
row.title: Group rotation, phase cadence, and no-repeat scheduling

row.description_md: When a group cannot fill the next round, the planner must use the global pool for that phase. It must preserve the seen ledger, notify the host, and restore groups in the next phase. The planner can merge or re-split groups only as a repair after participant loss. It must record the repair. A routine phase must not merge groups.
row.purpose_md: A phase failure does not stall or break the event.
row.reason_md: Group rotation can exhaust or become infeasible.
row.solution_idea_md: Add a global-pool fallback path, a host alert, an audit entry, and repair validation. Add tests for infeasible phases and merge repair.
row.title: Infeasible phase fallback and merge repair

row.description_md: Select the next offer from one global queue. A participant must be Active and Ready and must not have an active offer. A track must not be their own track, a track they have seen, or a track with an active offer. Prefer a track whose owner or latest holder the participant has not worked with. Return one deterministic choice per participant. Do not use group labels or a precomputed classic plan.
row.purpose_md: The async mode needs a scalable queue that avoids repeats and familiar pairs.
row.reason_md: Async has no scheduler.
row.solution_idea_md: Add a pure async queue module with candidate and pair-history inputs. Use a deterministic score and tie-break. Add property and unit tests.
row.title: Async queue selection and diversity score

row.description_md: Create one offer per ready participant from the async queue. The offer contains the track code and the claim deadline and no file. The claim window is 24 hours by default. Send one claim reminder with 12 hours left. An expired offer returns the track, does not mark the pair as seen, pauses the participant for the Ready gate, and never offers that track to that person again. Record the wave and expiry in the audit log.
row.purpose_md: The async loop must start, remind, and expire without loops.
row.reason_md: The queue needs the durable offer pipeline.
row.solution_idea_md: Add an async dispatch engine function and host command. Reuse the assignment and delivery outbox. Add expiry and reminder handling to the deadline tick. Add tests for dispatch, claim reminder, expiry, and no re-offer.
row.title: Async offer dispatch, expiry protection, and claim reminder

row.description_md: Use N-1 rounds for 12 or fewer participants and a 6 to 8 round cap above 12. Report exposed and unexposed participant-track pairs at the end. List each gap with a reason. Do not promise edit completeness. Add the late-seed minimum editor quota.
row.purpose_md: The host must see the planned exposure and the actual gaps.
row.reason_md: The async mode has no length or coverage model.
row.solution_idea_md: Add a pure length policy and a coverage report from assignments and seen pairs. Add tests for small, capped, and late-seed events.
row.title: Async event length, coverage, and gap report

row.description_md: Run two dispatch waves in one daily release window. The default window starts at 18:00 local time. The second wave runs two hours later. Unclaimed offers shift when the host changes the release time. Claimed assignments keep their due date. A paused participant must tap Ready to resume. Do not use silent auto-advance.
row.purpose_md: The host and participants can predict the async rhythm.
row.reason_md: The queue needs a daily schedule and a resume path.
row.solution_idea_md: Add release time settings, a wave scheduler in the periodic worker, and host and participant Ready controls. Add tests for wave timing, shift, and resume.
row.title: Async two-wave schedule and Ready gate

row.description_md: R1 is the seed round and counts in the event length. A full-exposure classic event with N participants has N total rounds: R1 seed and R2..RN exchanges. The host opens R1 with the pack and a seed deadline, closes it softly, and locks the roster in one action. The planner shows a host-only R1 seed band and R2..RN exchange columns. File versions use v1..vN; rounds use R1..RN.
row.purpose_md: Remove the one-off round numbering and make round 1 the seed round.
row.reason_md: The current engine models seeds as a pre-round phase and calls the first exchange R1.
row.title: Classic round model: seed round, total length, and version naming

row.description_md: Each classic round has one shared deadline set when the host opens it. Offers expire at the round deadline and claims use the same deadline. Defaults are 7 days for R1, 24 hours for normal exchange rounds, and 48 hours for the final exchange round. The host can move a whole round deadline for all offered, claimed, and overdue assignments, preserve later individual extensions, return overdue to claimed, re-arm reminders, notify holders, and write one audit entry. Later planned rounds and the reveal shift by the same delta. Submitted work stays final.
row.purpose_md: Give the host honest round lengths and a single deadline that moves everyone.
row.reason_md: The current code gives each claim its own edit window and has no round deadline.
row.title: Classic shared round deadlines, final round, and whole-round moves

row.description_md: The host uploads the module pack (samples, no notes) and uploads are required by default; bring-your-own is configurable. At R1 open the bot DMs the pack to pre-signups and posts it in the channel. Late joiners during R1 receive it by DM. The pack has an ID, is stored locally, and is exposed to the UI only through an opaque ID. The pack must not pass bytes through IPC. Store and distribute now; sample reports are a separate follow-up.
row.purpose_md: Participants need the starting material for Round 1.
row.reason_md: The pack is currently an inert settings string.
row.title: Host pack upload, distribution, and seed-round gate

row.description_md: Participants can give unavailable date ranges. The planner must avoid assigning them during those ranges or mark the rounds as gaps. The host can fill gaps or choose a different plan. Availability changes must be audited. This works with the quantity-driven max_handoffs setting.
row.purpose_md: Match the schedule to when people can actually work.
row.reason_md: The join flow collects optional away dates, but the engine does not store or use them.
row.title: Date-driven participant availability

row.description_md: Add an explicit host setting for an open schedule. Open schedule means full transparency: participants see the R2..RN matrix, seed owners, editor names, titles, and comments before the reveal. The default stays own assignments only. The host sees a strong warning and the join card discloses the zero-anonymity exception. This is the only exception to anonymity until reveal.
row.purpose_md: Support groups who want a fully open event.
row.reason_md: The host asked for an explicit zero-anonymity option.
row.title: Open schedule transparency mode

row.description_md: Groups are a higher-order schedule. The host designs levels (groups, supergroups, arbitrary depth), chooses what moves at each level (participants, whole groups with tracks, or both), and gets recommendations and optimization presets. The builder must be intuitive, preview feasibility and fun, and avoid guaranteed infeasibility. Group membership stays hidden from participants. A first useful version can support a small number of levels with validation and manual overrides.
row.purpose_md: Let hosts design large events with meaningful social circles.
row.reason_md: The current group planner supports one level and one rotation rule.
row.title: Hierarchical group schedule builder and optimizer

row.description_md: The host chooses per event between strict full exposure and flexible participation. In strict mode every active participant must have max_handoffs at least N-1 for the exchange rounds; the seed is not an edit. In flexible mode the planner gives each participant their earliest available exchange rounds up to their cap, leaves gaps for skipped rounds, and the host can fill gaps with fill-ins or manual edits. Participants do not request specific tracks; the host edits manually. Date-driven availability is a separate issue.
row.purpose_md: Let hosts and participants trade exposure for capacity.
row.reason_md: max_handoffs is collected but unused, and full exposure conflicts with low caps.
row.title: Flexible participation with max_handoffs and coverage gaps

row.description_md: Research and simulate hierarchical group schedules for 12 to 1000 participants. Compare group sizes, hierarchy depths, rotation policies, cadences, and optimization objectives. Measure feasibility, exposure, pair and track diversity, repeats, own-track risk, gaps, runtime, and a fun proxy. Recommend what generalizes, the default hierarchy, the host controls, and a minimal first builder version.
row.purpose_md: Choose a hierarchical group model from evidence, not intuition.
row.reason_md: Full exposure is impossible at 1000 participants, and the current single-level model does not generalize.
row.title: Fun metric and 1000-participant schedule simulation

row.body_md: Formal verification decision (2026-11-25). Goals: find design bugs early and prevent invariant regressions. Friction: path-filtered PR job plus a deeper nightly; a failing model blocks release only for properties modeled at that release. v0.1.0 is blocked only by models that exist then (claim and parser proofs); schedule/async/delivery/reveal models are required before 1.0. Stack: TLA+/TLC, proptest-state-machine against the real engine, and Kani for parsers and custom IDs. First model: claim/offer/custody/expiry with a bounded logical clock and per-pair deadlines. Per-model runtime ceilings: 5 minutes on PR, 20 minutes nightly; if exceeded, reduce scope or use Apalache, never silently skip. Conformance: shared action vocabulary plus real-engine proptests; Tier 3 uses ITF replay after a spike, with NDJSON trace validation as fallback. Anonymity: projection tests, canary strings, outbound-effect audit, and log scans, not a TLA+ proof. Human owns property meaning; agents may update specs for mechanical drift. Every property must have a deliberately broken mutation that fails. Tools are pinned by checksum; the jar is not committed. Formal artifacts are dev-only, have zero product dependency, and can be deleted in one PR. Scripts are authoritative; the project-local skill is optional guidance. Formal checks are not architecture drivers. Coverage target: feature-aligned modules (Claim, Schedule, Async, Delivery, Reveal), then maintain; no open-ended expansion. No fixed maintenance budget, but a per-model runtime ceiling and a tracked waiver process prevent the program from becoming a hurdle. Full research and rationale: to be recorded in docs/FORMAL_METHODS.md when implementation starts.

Adopt none as a runtime dependency. Use the MIT best practices in a project-local skill after the spike; scripts and CI remain authoritative. Key pitfalls to guard: spec drift (record sync commits and map actions), vacuous properties (mandatory mutation), state explosion (small scopes and runtime ceilings), bounded-check complacency (state assumptions), and anonymity claims that TLA+ cannot support (use projection tests).

row.body_md: Scheduler algorithm scope: (1) randomized cyclic Latin square: build the canonical cyclic square, then permute rows (rounds), columns (tracks), and symbols (participants) with the event seed; (2) seeded row-by-row perfect matching, the current fallback; (3) balanced matching: min-cost max-flow with costs for repeated handoff pairs, recent encounters, uneven track exposure, and an own-track/seen-pair infeasible edge; (4) local-search improvement: swap two participants within a round only when both assignments stay valid and the balance metric improves; (5) repair: backtracking or min-cost flow with a Hall violator certificate, never relaxing no-repeat or own-track; (6) group rotation: split balanced groups, tracks stay in the original group, rotate people each K phases, fall back to the global pool for an infeasible phase, and log the repair; (7) balance metrics: max/min track exposure per participant, repeated handoff pairs, cross-group handoffs, group size ratio, and phase count. All strategies are deterministic for the same canonical input and seed. Strategy is selectable, default balanced. The demo matrix must use a seeded plan, not a cyclic shift.

row.body_md:
Second adversarial review found three must-fix defects. Fixed at e5cb624:

- MF-1: inbound handlers were spawned per event, so two submissions could commit out of message order. Each participant now has a FIFO queue. A queued attachment test proves version 2 then version 3.
- MF-2: a failed startup backfill was abandoned. The dispatcher now retries failed participants until they catch up, gates live work for those participants, writes one backfill.failed audit row, and alerts the host. A retry test proves the fetch failure is recovered.
